correctness.rationale: At most one source and one sink can exist. Repeatedly removing sources yields a canonical initial linear chain. Subsequent sink peeling from source-free residue cannot create a source because each remaining vertex already beat that sink; the nonempty terminal core has no global source or sink and at least three vertices. Two-variable formulas σ_i(x) and reversed θ_i(x) recursively define the ith head/tail positions via scoped variable reuse; fixed finite i needs only x,y, so different peeling counts and transitive lengths are distinguishable. For equal (h,t), Duplicator maps matching chain positions; inside a core, each vertex has both in- and out-neighbor, so a permanent two-pebble response preserves equality and either arc orientation for arbitrary moves and depth. No counting quantifier is used. A 3-cycle core gives minimal nontransitive representative, and any core size r>=3 exists (e.g. lexicographic blow-up of a 3-cycle), giving 1+C(n−1,2) classes. Independent enumeration of all labelled tournaments of orders 1..5 found invariant class counts [1,1,2,4,7], matching formula; finite checks cannot replace infinite-depth Duplicator argument.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks only establish the specific enumerated instances; unrestricted conclusion rests on mathematical proof.
